correctness.rationale: For each r-tuple, finite-field polynomial interpolation gives quotient generation iff the q-ary vertex labels are injective. For each arrow component, the image of the commutator hyperplane map must equal the entire arrow block: failure creates a proper ideal modulo which all inputs commute, but the quotient algebra does not; sufficiency follows by sandwiching the commutators between interpolated diagonal idempotent lifts. Restriction of an m by r matrix to a fixed r-1 dimensional hyperplane is onto in \(q^m\) times the product of factors \(q^{r-1}-q^j\). The independent word-span enumeration (F2,F3,F4) passed eleven cases and is corroborative, not the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The maximal-subalgebra theorem explains why vertex collisions and missing arrow directions are the failure modes. It does not state their exact joint probability, the independent full-rank product, or the sharp all-arity threshold. General generation estimates do not imply the exact fiber factors. value.rationale: The all-arity generation probability and minimum number of unital generators are natural algebraic invariants, and exact simultaneous evaluation for every finite loopless directed multiquiver and every finite field is a genuine classification rather than a single numerical example. The formula separates collision and parallel-arrow rank obstructions and gives a sharp generability threshold in arbitrarily large embedding dimensions. These are meaningful finite-algebra structural and probabilistic facts not provided by generic asymptotic bounds.
